cards.explanation: The answer is that he will be destroyed. Isaiah says, "When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed." The destroyer has been dishing it out, and now it comes back around to him. The traitor gets the same treatment: "…you will be betrayed." I think that guy never once pictured the line turning around.

The answer is False. The prayer says, "Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble." Strength is for every morning, friends, even the quiet ones. Salvation is the part that's asked for in time of trouble.

The answer is that they scatter. The verse says, "the nations scatter when You rise." Just before that, "The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice…" So when the LORD rises, the nations scatter and the peoples flee. I'd scatter too.

The answer is justice and righteousness. The verse says, "He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness." The same verse says the LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high. Filled is a big word, friends, because Zion isn't getting a sprinkle of it. It's getting a full measure.

The answer is the fear of the LORD. "The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure." Right before that, He's called "…a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge." So the treasure Isaiah names isn't something you can count.

The answer is that they weep bitterly. That's the verse: "the envoys of peace weep bitterly." These are the very people sent to make peace, and they're in tears. Right alongside them, the valiant ones cry aloud in the streets. It's a hard scene, and I think it hurts to read.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, "The treaty has been broken…" The same verse says the highways are deserted and travel has ceased. The verse doesn't say who broke it, only that it's broken. Empty roads and a broken treaty, all in one verse.

The answer is that they are despised. Isaiah says, "…the witnesses are despised…" The same verse says the treaty has been broken and "…human life is disregarded." Despised is a heavy word, friends, and I think this verse hurts to read.

The answer is leaves. "Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves." Bashan and Carmel are places in the land, and here they're dropping leaves as the land mourns. The same verse says Sharon is like a desert. It's a sad picture of a land that's worn out.
The answer is right now. The word is "Now." The LORD says, "Now I will arise…" and then, "Now I will lift Myself up. Now I will be exalted." He says it three times in a row. I'd say He means it.

The answer is consume. The LORD says, "Your breath is a fire that will consume you." He says it to the ones who conceive chaff and give birth to stubble. It's a hard verse, so I'll say it plainly: the fire is called their own breath.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "The peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze." It's a serious verse, friends. The verse before it says, "You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble."
The answer is False. The LORD says, "You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might." He calls the far off and the near. So it's for everybody.

The answer is who can dwell with everlasting flames. "Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?" The sinners in Zion are afraid, and trembling grips the ungodly. It's a question that comes out of fear.
The answer is True. This person is described as one "…whose hand never takes a bribe…" He also "…refuses gain from extortion…" His hands stay clean.
The answer is that he stops his ears against them. The verse says, "…who stops his ears against murderous plots…" He also "…shuts his eyes tightly against evil…" He won't listen and he won't look.

The answer is the mountain fortress. Isaiah says, "the mountain fortress will be his refuge…" That's about the one who walks righteously, who will dwell on the heights. A fortress up there sounds a lot better than a leaky tent.

The answer is False. The text says, "his food will be provided and his water assured." Provided and assured are the words Isaiah uses for his food and water. That same verse puts him on the heights, with the mountain fortress as his refuge.

The answer is the King in His beauty. That's the promise: "Your eyes will see the King in His beauty…" Isaiah is talking about seeing the King with your own eyes. And he adds a land that stretches afar.
The answer is True. Isaiah says they will "…behold a land that stretches afar." That comes right after seeing the King in His beauty. A whole wide land, in view.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "You will no longer see the insolent, a people whose speech is unintelligible, who stammer in a language you cannot understand." No longer means no more, friends. They'll be gone from sight.
The answer is wander. Jerusalem is "…a tent that does not wander…" Its tent pegs won't be pulled up, and its cords won't be broken. This tent stays put.

The answer is the LORD. Isaiah says, "…the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals…" The place isn't a king or a city on its own. The LORD Himself is that place for them. The next verse says, "For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King."
The answer is that He will save them. Isaiah says, "It is He who will save us." The LORD is their Judge, their lawgiver and their King. Three titles, and the verse lands on one promise.

The answer is even the lame. Isaiah says, "…even the lame will carry off plunder." It comes right after he says an abundance of spoils will be divided. The lame are the ones he names as carrying it off.

The answer is that it is forgiven. Isaiah says, "The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity." That's how the chapter ends, friends. Right before it, he says no resident of Zion will say, "I am sick."
